text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Proving its seriousness in ridding itself of money politics, the ruling United Malays National Organisation has disqualified six candidates from contesting supreme council posts and another for the executive council of its youth wing at this week's general assembly.
-- A Filipina maid has accused the ambassador of a Balkan state, who is her employer, of raping her on four occassions since April 11.
-- Malaysia and Indonesia have decided to refer their territorial dispute over Sipadan and Ligitan islands to the International Court of Justice for arbitration.
-- The Shah Alam Municipal Council has rejected an application to hold the Michael Jackson concert at its stadium on October 27.
-- Malaysia and Indonesia are working on an ambitious proposal to build a bridge across the Straits of Malacca to link Peninsular Malaysia and north Sumatra.
-- The government will go ahead with its proposal to set up an independent framework to regulate accounting practices in Malaysia despite protests from accountants.

-- The implementation of the recent amendments to the Companies Act which require companies to state their reference number in all official documents has been postponed until end of this year, Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Abu Hassan Omar said.
